where_words_note: How a person reads each `where` value, as the end of a phrase (`on your word <words>`, `answered <words>`), read by question_register.where_words (FR-13). Every value of `where` has a row in `where_words`; a value this file does not know is read as `earlier`. `gate A` and `gate B` keep the form they have always had on the gate cards (`at gate A`). The `S4 stop` row is added together with the `S4 stop` value of `where` (HF2-7 part P5a).

where_words.S3 stop: while the test plan was written
where_words.S4 stop: while the test cases were written
where_words.conductor: in an answer you gave in the chat

risk_word_note: The one word of gate B that orders a delivery over a verdict that is not yes: read by question_register.risk_reason_of ONLY as a whole line of its own, the word alone or followed by `:` and the person's reason (FR-12, FR-13). Any other form is the conductor's reading, never a phrase search in code.

stand_gap_words.note: The one-word answers to a stand-gap card at gate B, written on a line of their own as `<case id>: <word>` (gate_brief.read_stand_gap_answers reads them; the driver then records the person's word with the same command the card used to print). CLOSED and ENGLISH ONLY on purpose (FR-13, owner 02.10): a person answers in their own language, and any wording that is not `word` or one of `synonyms` - in any language - is not read by code: it goes to the conductor, which maps it to this form. `option` is the value contract.STAND_GAP_OPTIONS keeps in the record (it is what `stand_gap_decisions` reads back); `word` is what the card shows; `says` is the card's explanation. Matching is on the WHOLE text after the colon, lower-cased, with backquotes, quotes and a closing . or ! removed and runs of spaces collapsed. A word or synonym may belong to one option only. A row with `lasting: true` (`accept always`, B-414) is the option `accept` with a longer life - the project's environment record keeps it (D-0029); it is read only for a gap that has a key to record it under (never for a gap whose cause is a file or the machine, D-0032), listed only while an open card offers it, and left out of every reader that maps an option to ONE word (gate_brief.stand_gap_words(lasting=True) returns it; the default list does not). A level gap (every test of one execution contour) is answered by its contour: `<level name>: <word>`.

answers.says: I make the change shown above, on your word
you run this test yourself, where the missing piece exists
it stays blocked and is reported as not run
the same as `accept` for this story, and the project's environment record keeps it, so no story asks it again until what it was recorded for changes or you take it back

exploratory_question_words.note: The one-word answers to a QUESTION LINE of the exploratory findings at gate B (`Questions for you - is this intended?`), written on a line of their own as `<case id>: <word>` (gate_brief.read_exploratory_answers reads them with the stand-gap reader's grammar; the driver then carries each one out: `intended` confirms the line and its question, `bug` sends the failure analysis back with the person's words, `open` leaves it with the person). CLOSED and ENGLISH ONLY on purpose (FR-13, FR-12): any other wording, in any language, is not read by code - it goes to the conductor. `option` is `intended`, `bug` or `open`; `word` is what the packet shows; `says` is the packet's explanation; `factory`, `you` and `story` are the three price lines the packet prints under the option (human-questions.md item 6). Matching is on the WHOLE text after the colon, lower-cased, with backquotes, quotes and a closing . or ! removed and runs of spaces collapsed. A word or synonym belongs to one option of one reader only: no word here is a word of stand_gap_words, environment_words, probe_answers, gate-approval-words.json, the case decisions, `not needed` or `until the report` (a test holds the files apart).

answers.says: what was seen is the expected behaviour; it is recorded with your words and is not a bug
answers.factory: a record only; no agent works.
answers.story: the expectation is confirmed by you; delivery unchanged.

answers.says: what was seen is wrong; the failure analysis runs again with your words as the expectation, and a bug follows its usual road
answers.factory: the failure analysis and everything after it run again.
answers.you: this answer, and one more look at this gate.
answers.story: delivery waits until the gate is shown again.

answers.you: deciding it later, outside the factory.
answers.story: it stays in the report's findings as left open with you; delivery unchanged.

attachment_question_words.note: The two answers of the attachments block of gate A (gate_brief._attachment_lines, FR-13): `nothing_to_add` is read with gate A's approval word (the word is data of gate-approval-words.json, never written here); `own_words` is answered in the person's own words, which the conductor turns into a rework of S2. `{word}` in a `says` is that approval word, and `says_without_word` is the sentence when gate A has none (FR-59). Each row carries the three price lines of human-questions.md item 6. NOT in question-prices.json: a key rendered from gate_brief makes K15 red.

nothing_to_add.says: nothing to add; this also approves the plan and the cases as they stand
nothing_to_add.says_without_word: say that there is nothing to add
nothing_to_add.factory: a record only; no agent works.
nothing_to_add.story: what stands only in these attachments is not checked; the delivery verdict stays as the report has it.

own_words.says: say which requirement, in your own words, instead of `{word}`
own_words.says_without_word: say which requirement, in your own words
own_words.factory: a helper reads your words and offers you the choices; then the requirements stage (S2) and the stages after it run again up to this gate.
own_words.you: this answer, one more answer to choose, and one more look at this gate.
own_words.story: delivery waits until the gate is shown again.

environment_words.note: The word about what the project's environment record (qa-factory/records/environment-properties.json) holds, read by gate_brief.read_stand_gap_answers ONLY against a gap the record covers - a gap with no card, listed in the block `Decided once for this environment` - into `revokes`, never into `read` (B-414). `revoke` takes the record's row back: later gates ask the gap again; the stories that already answered it keep their own answers. Matching is the same as for stand_gap_words, and a word or synonym may not belong to both lists.

answers.says: the environment record forgets this answer, and the gap is asked again at every gate

finding_door_words.note: The words a rehearsal finding's OWN door takes besides the stand-gap answers, read ONLY by story_run.Driver.read_finding_doors, for a finding whose door option is the row's option (gate_brief.finding_door_words). The word may be followed by a separator and the person's reason, which is kept whole. The list is closed and English only (FR-13). A word or synonym of this block belongs to no other block of this file, and a test holds them apart.

answers.says: the product has no such function: the requirement is reported as not implemented and the delivery is not ready

probe_answers.note: The answers of a stand-gap card about a test command that writes no report (the gate A reporter card, B-220 part 2) that are NOT one of stand_gap_words, read by gate_brief.read_stand_gap_answers: `command` is the word followed by the person's own command line, written as they would type it (the REST of the line, case kept; one pair of backquotes round the whole value is peeled; a value that ends in one of `continuation_marks` is not read - the command may go on in a line that is not here; at most 1000 characters, which is what `value` says). The other answers a reporter card takes are the existing words `myself`, `run`, `accept`, and `change` - but `change` only while `live` is true AND report-cures.json holds a cure that is one change of that command. `live` says whether the factory EXECUTES the two answers that change the command: a `command` line (the driver probes it, asks one `Do it?` and applies it only on the person's recorded yes) and `change` (the same path, for the cure the card shows): false until those handlers exist, and while it is false (this release) a reporter card offers exactly `myself`, `run`, `accept`, and a line that uses `command` or `change` is not read - an offered word nobody executes would pass the card on a promise (FR-9). `reporter_accept` is the line a card about such a test command adds under the list of words, to say what `accept` means there. A `value` that is not a regular expression drops the row and the reader names why (`problem`).

command.says: you give the command line that makes this test command write a report, written after the word as you would type it; I try it first, and I ask you once more before I change anything
command.note: offered only for a card about a test command that writes no report

probe_answers.reporter_accept: On a card about a test command that writes no report, `accept` means the factory goes on without that report: the tests of that command cannot be read, so the report lists them as not run.
